newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures drop after hurricane falters.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures drop after hurricane falters.

text.p: IPE oil futures dropped sharply on Friday on reports a U.S. Gulf hurricane would not hit production as hard as originally feared, brokers said.
September IPE Brent was down 44 cents at $18.27 a barrel at 16.43 gmt, having fallen sharply in the late afternoon, busting through the major support level of $18.45.
August IPE gas oil trade closed down $3.50 a tonne at $163.50, as the whole oil complex was brought lower by feverish selling in New York, where August NYMEX crude was down 54 cents.
"The heat went out of the market with the news the hurricane wasn't going to hit things as badly as feared," a broker said.
IPE Brent's next support was $18.25 a barrel, which it broke through before returning a little higher. If it breaks through conclusively the next downward target is $17.80, brokers said.
"All eyes now will be on whether it can recover and close above $18.45," said one broker.

Oil companies who evacuated personnel from U.S. Gulf rigs and installations ahead of Hurricane Danny were sending crews back to work after the storm passed across the Louisiana coast with relatively little incident.
The storm and news of supply problems in the North Sea had pushed the market higher on Thursday.

Unleaded gasoline, which helped push the market higher earlier in the week after bearish industry stock data showed a four million barrel draw, had already been coming off before it was clear the hurricane threat had receded.
By late afternoon unleaded futures were down 1.44 cents at 60.55 cents a gallon, helping to drive IPE values lower.
"There were a lot of stops hit in the States which brought things down," said one broker. "This is a purely NYMEX driven market now."

Production problems at the North Sea Nelson field have hit July loadings in the Forties system, with at least one cargo deferred, but brokers said this factor was overwhelmed by the bearish wave of selling triggered by the U.S.
